questions.q: Transform into negative: 'He is always honest.'
questions.explanation: Affirmative 'always honest' becomes 'never dishonest' in negative.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Transform into negative: 'As soon as he saw the tiger, he fled.'
options: No sooner did he see the tiger than he fled.
As soon as he didn't see tiger.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' transforms to 'No sooner did... than...'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Transform into affirmative: 'There is no smoke without fire.'
options: Where there is smoke, there is fire.
questions.explanation: Negative 'no smoke without fire' transforms to conditional affirmative.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Transform into comparative degree: 'Iron is the most useful metal.'
options: Iron is more useful than any other metal.
questions.explanation: Superlative 'most useful' transforms to 'more useful than any other'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Transform into positive degree: 'Kolkata is larger than most other cities in India.'
options: No city is large as Kolkata.
Very few cities in India are as large as Kolkata.
Kolkata is as large as city.
questions.explanation: Comparative with 'most other' transforms to 'Very few... as large as'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Transform into assertive: 'What a beautiful flower this is!'
options: This is a very beautiful flower.
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentence transforms to assertive 'This is a very...'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Transform into exclamatory: 'I wish I were a king.'
options: O that I were a king!
questions.explanation: Assertive wish transforms to 'O that I were...' or 'Would that...'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Combine into single simple sentence: 'He heard the noise. He woke up.'
options: As he heard noise he woke.
Hearing the noise, he woke up.
questions.explanation: Participle combination: 'Hearing the noise, he woke up.'
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Combine into compound sentence: 'He worked hard. He failed.'
options: He worked hard, but he failed.
questions.explanation: Adversative conjunction 'but' combines contrasting clauses.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Combine into complex sentence: 'He is poor. He is honest.'
options: Although he is poor, he is honest.
questions.explanation: Subordinating conjunction 'Although' forms a complex sentence.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'Put out' mean?

questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'Bring up' mean?

questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'Carry out' mean?

questions.q: Find the error: 'He has been suffering with fever since Monday.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'suffering' takes preposition 'from'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'She is more cleverer than her sister.'
questions.explanation: Comparative 'cleverer' does not require 'more'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'The sceneries of Kashmir are breathtaking.'
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun with no plural form.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'I prefer tea than coffee.'
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by preposition 'to'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'He did not went to school yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Auxiliary 'did' must be followed by base verb V1 'go'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'Each of the students have submitted their project.'
questions.explanation: Distributive subject 'Each' requires singular verb 'has'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'Sun rises in east.'
questions.explanation: Unique celestial bodies and cardinal directions take article 'The'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'He is senior than me.'
questions.explanation: 'Senior' takes preposition 'to'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'Neither Ram nor his brothers is present.'
questions.explanation: Verb agrees with nearest plural subject 'brothers' -> 'are'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Find the error: 'I am reading this book for two hours.'
questions.explanation: Action starting in past and continuing takes present perfect continuous.
questions.subject: English

questions.explanation: Virtue (moral goodness) is opposite to vice.
